llm.summary: The skill mostly implements what it claims (memory augmentation and optional Zhipu API integration), but there are multiple metadata/requirement inconsistencies and a few behaviors (file writes, external API calls) you should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code and SKILL.md implement memory retrieval, augmentation, and LLM-call interception via the Memori library and optionally the Zhipu API, which matches the skill name/description. However, registry metadata lists ZHIPUAI_API_KEY and ZHIPUAI_MODEL as required environment variables while the SKILL.md and README mark them optional; SKILL.md also contains metadata that sets user-invocable to false while the registry flags user-invocable as true. These mismatches between declared requirements and documentation are inconsistent and should be resolved.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code show the skill will: read and write a local database (default ./memori.db), load tech terms from MEMORI_TECH_TERMS or a file (MEMORI_TECH_TERMS_FILE), optionally call the Zhipu API sending conversation text, and support persisting added tech terms to disk. Those actions are within scope for a memory/interceptor skill, but they involve reading/writing files and sending conversation content to an external API (Zhipu) — the user should be aware and only provide API keys if they consent to that external transmission.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (no downloads or extract steps) — the skill expects Python and pip packages (memori and optionally zhipuai) to be installed. This is low-risk compared to arbitrary remote downloads, but the SKILL.md instructs pip installs that must be performed by the operator; the package sources are standard PyPI names (no unknown URLs present).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry lists ZHIPUAI_API_KEY and ZHIPUAI_MODEL as required env vars even though the SKILL.md/README describe them as optional. The code also reads MEMORI_TECH_TERMS and MEMORI_TECH_TERMS_FILE environment variables (not declared in the registry 'required env' list). Requiring an external API key when the integration is optional is disproportionate and the undeclared environment variables reduce transparency. Note: supplying ZHIPUAI_API_KEY enables sending conversation content to a third-party service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill may create/modify local files: a memori DB (default ./memori.db) and the tech terms file (MEMORI_TECH_TERMS_FILE) if persist is used. It does not request 'always: true'. Autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation: false) is normal; combined with ability to persist config and call an external API, this increases blast radius if you give it an API key — consider limiting permissions or testing in a sandbox first.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Things to check before installing/using this skill:

- Metadata mismatch: the registry marks ZHIPUAI_API_KEY/ZHIPUAI_MODEL as required while the SKILL.md/README mark them optional. Confirm whether you must provide an API key — do not supply secrets unless you intend the skill to send conversation data to Zhipu.

- Undeclared env vars: the code also uses MEMORI_TECH_TERMS and MEMORI_TECH_TERMS_FILE (for reading/writing tech-term configuration) but these are not listed as required in registry metadata; review/decide where that file will live and its permissions.

- Data sent externally: if you provide ZHIPUAI_API_KEY the skill will build prompts containing conversation text and send them to Zhipu. Do not provide an API key if you do not want conversation content transmitted to a third party.

- Local persistence: by default the skill will open/create a database at ./memori.db and can append to a tech terms file. If you have sensitivity about local files, set explicit paths and verify where files are written.

- Installation: there is no automated installer; you must pip install the memori package (and zhipuai only if you want augmentation). Review the memori and zhipuai packages (source, versions) before installing.

- Code completeness: the provided memori_extension.py listing was truncated in the review, which reduces confidence. Inspect the full source on disk (or from the publisher) before enabling the skill.

- Recommended test approach: run the skill in a restricted/sandboxed environment first (no Zhipu API key, no network or with monitoring), verify file paths and behavior, then decide whether to supply optional API credentials and enable broader privileges.
